summary.intent: Compare the interactive CLI first-release experience of real @changesets/cli 3.0.3 against callisto 0.22.0 using real pty transcripts (trail #487), put the table and transcripts in the PR body, and implement only the clearly helpful, dialoguer-compatible gaps in `callisto add`.
summary.outcome: Captured pty transcripts of both tools and rewrote the `callisto add` wizard (changed packages first and preselected, per-package bump prompts, review before writing, next-step line, Esc cancel, $EDITOR summary, paging), updating unit tests, docs/specs/cli.json and adding a minor changeset. The work was committed (signing needed an out-of-sandbox retry); the push, PR body with comparison table, trail link and report to the lead are not yet done.

repo: The changed-package derivation is `callisto_graph::changed::changed_since_last_tag`, the same one `status` uses; `add` reuses it so the wizard matches reported state.
Package names in the wizard use `pkg.id.display_name()` so `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` stay distinct in polyglot workspaces.
Spec criteria in docs/specs/cli.json must be updated together with behaviour changes.
`just lint` and `cargo test -p callisto-cli` are the local checks; 4 e2e tests fail in the sandbox because of an npm cache EPERM and blocked crates.io/uv network, not because of `add`.
Ctrl-C under dialoguer/console exits immediately and can leave the cursor hidden, while Esc is handled and restores it; this was documented in the changeset.

code.finding: `run_wizard` now takes `&[Choice]` (name plus changed flag), orders changed packages first and ticks them via `MultiSelect::defaults`. It then asks major, then minor (the rest are patch), then summary, then a preview with confirm. The `AddPrompter` trait gained prompt and checked params so tests script it, and `wizard_choices` replaced `collect_package_names`.
The spec criterion describing the add wizard was updated to match the new prompts.

workflow: Sandbox denies pty allocation ('out of pty devices'), so the pty driver must run outside the sandbox.
Changesets needs a lockfile (`npm install` in the fixture) to discover workspace packages.
Signed commits need gpg, so the commit has to run outside the sandbox; a `git merge origin/main` right before pushing was a no-op here.
The `rtk` wrapper and plain `git` behaved inconsistently, so `/usr/bin/git` was used directly.
Moving fixture setup into scripts (setup.sh, try.sh, new.sh) and JSON keystroke files made pty runs repeatable.

friction: pty allocation blocked in the sandbox; every driver run needed escalation.
npm cache and network restrictions in the sandbox forced a custom cache dir and caused unrelated test failures.
Changesets found no packages until the fixture had a lockfile, which cost several fixture-rewrite iterations.
Esc/Ctrl-C driver runs initially did not wait for the child to exit, so drive.py needed a wait loop to capture cursor state.
The lead raised the bar mid-task (theme, paging, review screen, editor summary, Esc cancel), expanding scope.
open_items: Push the branch with `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, confirm with ls-remote, link trail #487 and open the PR with `entire trail ci-pr`.
Write the PR body (comparison table and real transcripts) via `gh pr edit --body-file`.
`callisto init` theming is planned as a second PR.
Ctrl-C can still leave the cursor hidden; only documented, not fixed.
Run `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the new decision logic if the lead wants it.
Report to the lead in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what was run.
